title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.4). G is the (motivic or Mumford–Tate type) group whose Tannakian category Rep(G) is under study. i: G_m -> G is the weight cocharacter, so the Q-grading by degree n comes from i. ε: G -> G_m is the character giving Q(1), normalised so that ε∘i(λ) = λ^2. A homomorphism j: S -> G_R, with S the Deligne torus Res_{C/R} G_m, induces a Hodge structure on every V in Rep(G). Conditions from p.4: (a) j restricted to G_{m,R} equals i_R; (b) ε∘j = Norm, so that Q(1) has bidegree (-1,-1) up to sign conventions. For V of degree n, a G-invariant form φ: V⊗V -> Q(-n) is a polarization iff φ_R(x, Cy) is symmetric positive definite, where C = j(√-1) is the Weil operator. Since C^2 = j(-1) = i(-1) acts by (-1)^n, φ is alternating for n odd and symmetric for n even.

NB (structure lemma). Put G' = Ker ε. Then G ≅ G' ×_{Z/2} G_{m,Q}, where Z/2 -> G' is i restricted to μ_2 and η = i(-1). So G, together with i and ε, is recovered from the pair (G', η). Likewise, j satisfying (a) and (b) is the same thing as h' = j|_U: U -> G'_R with h'(-1) = η, where U is the circle group.

Theorem. For j satisfying (a) and (b), the following are equivalent:
(i) every homogeneous V in Rep(G) carries a G-invariant polarization;
(ibis) some given V_α carry G-invariant polarizations, G -> Π Aut(V_α) is injective, and G' (equivalently G) is reductive;
(ii), (iibis) the same statements over R, i.e. for G_R and Rep(G_R).
These imply (iii): G'_R is reductive, and the centralizer K(j) of C = j(i) in G'^0_R is a maximal compact subgroup. Equivalently, the image of K(j) in G^0_R / i(R^{*+}) is maximal compact.

A rotated margin note tries to give equivalent forms of (iii):
- passing to G modulo centre (an adjoint quotient G'');
- passing to a quotient of G by a finite subgroup of G'.

In modern terms this is the criterion: all of Rep(G) is polarizable iff ad j(i) is a Cartan involution of G'_R (≈ G_R/w(G_m)). Equivalently, the j(i)-twisted real form is compact, and the centralizer of j(i) is maximal compact.

Purpose. The next page defines a 'G-subordination rigidifiée' on an analytic space S: a ⊗-functor from Rep(G) to real-analytically varying polarizable Hodge structures with holomorphic Hodge filtration, i.e. a variation of Hodge structure with G-structure. Pointwise this is a map s ↦ j'(s) satisfying the theorem's conditions. The classifying space is thus G'(R)/K, which is the Mumford–Tate / period-domain / Shimura-datum picture.
errors: Not an error: the reductivity hypothesis in (ibis) is redundant. A faithful polarizable V forces G'_R into a group stable under the Cartan involution ad C of GL(V_R). G' is stable under ad C because C ∈ G(R), and an algebraic subgroup stable under a Cartan involution is reductive. Grothendieck adds it as an explicit hypothesis ('De plus, on suppose G' réductif').

Grothendieck only claims (i)-(ii) ⇒ (iii), not an equivalence. In fact, for connected reductive G'_R with C^2 central, 'the centralizer of C is maximal compact' is equivalent to 'ad C is a Cartan involution' (it forces the centre to be anisotropic). So the converse holds with the right connectedness and component hypotheses. The margin's attempts at reformulation ('iiibis', 'iiiter') are unfinished.

Sign/normalisation conventions (bidegree of Q(1), C = j(i) versus j(i)^{-1}) are not fixed explicitly. This is harmless, since C and C^{-1} differ by C^2 = (-1)^n and so give the same positivity condition on homogeneous V.

ideas.what: Hodge structures on all of Rep(G) are given by a homomorphism j: S -> G_R with j|G_m = weight cocharacter and ε∘j = Norm. The Weil operator is C = j(i), and polarization means φ(x, Cy) is positive definite.
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of Hodge structures via h: S -> G_R (Mumford–Tate formalism)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford 1966 (Hodge/Mumford–Tate groups); Deligne 1971 (Travaux de Shimura; Théorie de Hodge II); Saavedra Rivano 1972

ideas.what: G ≅ G' ×_{μ2} G_m with G' = Ker(ε). Hodge data j correspond to h': U -> G'_R with h'(-1) = i(-1).
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of the Mumford–Tate group as Hodge group times weight torus; restriction of h to the circle group U
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford 1966 (Hodge group = special Mumford–Tate group); Deligne 1971/1979

ideas.what: Theorem: every representation is polarizable ⇔ a faithful family is polarizable (with G reductive) ⇔ the same over R ⇒ the centralizer of j(i) in G'^0_R is maximal compact.
ideas.modern_name: Polarizability criterion: ad h(i) is a Cartan involution of G/w(G_m) (Shimura datum axiom SV2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Travaux de Shimura (Sém. Bourbaki 1971) and Variétés de Shimura (1979) 2.1.1.2; Deligne–Milne 1982; Satake for related Kuga fibre space results (1965–66)

ideas.what: Using this pointwise criterion to define families: 'G-subordinations' on an analytic space, with classifying space G'(R)/K (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Variations of Hodge structure with G-structure; Mumford–Tate domains / Shimura data / period domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths 1968–70 (period domains); Deligne 1971/1979 (Shimura varieties); Green–Griffiths–Kerr (Mumford–Tate domains, 2012)

missed.claim: In 1965, in Tannakian language, Grothendieck states the equivalence 'every V in Rep(G) polarizable ⇔ a faithful V polarizable ⇔ the centralizer of the Weil operator j(i) in Ker(ε)_R is maximal compact'. This is essentially the Cartan-involution criterion that the literature attributes to Deligne (1971/1979) and that became axiom SV2 for Shimura data. This predates Mumford's 1966 Mumford–Tate paper and Saavedra's Tannakian formalism.
missed.quote: les conditions suivantes (i) (ii) (ibis) (iibis) sont équivalentes et impliquent (iii) ... le centralisateur de C dans G'°_R est un ss-groupe compact maximal
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point. The Mumford–Tate / Cartan-involution formalism underlying Shimura varieties and Mumford–Tate domains was formulated by Grothendieck, in the motivic Galois group context, by 1965. That suggests Deligne's later axiomatics had a direct Grothendieck antecedent.

missed.claim: The page links the motivic Galois group (Tannakian Rep(G)) directly to real Lie theory. Polarizability of motives/Hodge realizations becomes a compactness condition. Families of such structures (next page) are parametrized by G'(R)/K. This makes the bridge 'motivic Galois group → symmetric spaces/period domains' explicit in 1965.
missed.quote: h : S → G_R satisfaisant a) et b) équivaut à la donnée d'un hom h' : U → G'_R satisfaisant h'(-1) = η
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly absorbed by the later literature (Deligne, Green–Griffiths–Kerr). It is chiefly a historical record of where the idea originated, not a new mathematical result.

missed.claim: The margin attempts reformulations of (iii): via G/Centre ≅ G'' and via a quotient of G by a finite subgroup of G'. The intent is to reduce polarizability to the adjoint group modulo finite central isogeny. These are left incomplete.
missed.quote: NB (iii) équivaut aux conditions : (iiibis) G°/Centre ... (iiiter) ∃ un quotient de G par un ss-gr fini de G', tel que ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Low. The modern statement (Cartan involution on G^ad, plus a compact centre condition on G/w(G_m)) settles it.

deep.surprise_reason: The criterion itself is now textbook (Deligne 1971/79, Deligne–Milne). Finding it stated in Tannakian form in Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois notes is still a notable unpublished priority detail. So is the G-structured variation of Hodge structure on the next page, which predates Mumford–Tate and Deligne's Shimura data. It is not new mathematics today.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, the homomorphism is written 'j' in the manuscript (as on neighbouring pages), not 'h'. So: 'Pour j donné', 'C = j(i)', 'K(j)', 'j : S → G_R', 'j' : U → G'_R satisfaisant j'(-1) = η'.
In (i), the form is 'une polarisation (pour la structure de Hodge associée à j sur V), i.e. une forme : C = j(i)', with a closing bracket.
In (iii), the marginal arrow reads roughly 'composante connexe du groupe G^°_R' attached to the G^°_R in the line above.
The bracket reads 'Ceci implique que φ est alternée si n impair, symétrique si n pair'; this is correct.
